findings.summary: `.values(input)` passes a nested wrapper object `{ projectId, settings: {...} }` instead of flattened column values, causing the insert to only set projectId and drop the settings data on first insert
findings.failure_scenario: User edits project commands in settings UI, saves → client calls upsert with `{projectId: "abc", settings: {projectId: "abc", runCommand: "yarn dev", ...}}` → Drizzle's `.values(input)` sees only `projectId` as a matching column, ignores the `settings` key entirely → first insert creates a row with `run_command='', build_command='', install_command=''` (all defaults) → `returning()` returns this broken row → on next page load, `restoreProjectSettings` fetches the broken row → user's saved commands are overwritten with empty strings

findings.summary: `createCommit` sets `this.isSaving = true` then falls through the try block without any commit logic and without returning a result, causing the function to return `undefined` — all callers interpret `undefined` as a failure
findings.failure_scenario: User clicks 'New backup' button → `createCommit()` runs → `isSaving` guard passes → `isSaving = true` → no actual commit creation happens → try block ends → finally sets `isSaving = false` → function returns `undefined` → caller checks `!res?.success` → `!undefined?.success` is `true` → caller logs error and shows failure toast 'Failed to create commit'

findings.summary: Fallback chain duplicates `domainsManager.domains.preview?.url` twice instead of falling through to `domainsManager.domains.custom?.url`; custom domain URL is never used as a fallback
findings.failure_scenario: Project has a published custom domain with no preview domain → `baseUrl` resolves to `project?.sandbox.url` (the sandbox URL) since both preview references are null → page metadata saves the sandbox URL instead of the user-visible custom domain → OpenGraph metadata points visitors to the sandbox URL instead of the published custom domain

findings.summary: When `baseUrl` is `undefined`, `baseUrl?.startsWith('http')` returns `undefined` (falsy), constructing `"https://undefined"` which is truthy, so `new URL("https://undefined")` creates a URL with hostname "undefined"
findings.failure_scenario: New project with no domains configured (no preview, no custom, no sandbox) → `baseUrl` is `undefined` → url becomes `"https://undefined"` → `new URL("https://undefined")` succeeds with hostname "undefined" → `metadataBase` saved as `new URL('https://undefined')` → generated code exports `metadataBase: new URL("https://undefined")` which is a corrupt metadata value

findings.summary: Same URL-from-undefined pattern as site/index.tsx: when `baseUrl` is `undefined`, produces `new URL("https://undefined")`
findings.failure_scenario: Same as site/index.tsx — corrupt `metadataBase` when no domain URL is available for a page's metadata

findings.summary: `useEffect` resets `title` and `description` to `initialMetadata` values whenever `initialMetadata` reference changes, silently overwriting in-progress user edits regardless of the `isDirty` flag
findings.failure_scenario: User types a new title into the metadata form → parent component re-renders, creating a new `initialMetadata` object reference (with the same values) → `useEffect` fires → `setTitle` and `setDescription` are called with the original values → user's unsaved edit is silently discarded → user sees their typed text replaced with the old value mid-typing

findings.summary: `checkoutCommit` shows toast.success('Restored to backup!') and returns `true` after `createCommit` succeeds, but never actually checks out or restores any commit — the restore functionality is marked `// TODO: Implement`
findings.failure_scenario: User selects a backup to restore → `checkoutCommit` is called → `createCommit` returns success (once fixed) → toast shows 'Restored to backup!' → method returns `true` → no actual checkout or file restoration occurs → user believes their project was restored but nothing changed

findings.summary: `skipBuild: false` was removed from custom domain deployment options but remains in preview domain section — if the deploy service defaults `skipBuild` to `true`, custom domain deployments would skip the build step
findings.failure_scenario: User clicks 'Publish to custom domain' with a hosting provider where `skipBuild` defaults to `true` → build step is skipped for custom domain deployment → stale previously-built files are deployed to the live custom domain → meanwhile preview domain deploys fresh content (since `skipBuild: false` is still present there) → production site runs old content while preview shows new content
